summary.text: Matthew Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District and the sitting Maine State Auditor. A former journalist and columnist, he served in the Maine House, as Secretary of State in two separate stretches, and ran for U.S. Senate in 2012; he won the 2026 Democratic primary after a ranked-choice runoff.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Bar Harbor, Maine, and graduated from Mount Desert Island High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history (1987) and a master's degree in English literature (1994) from the University of Maine; also completed Harvard University's Senior Executives in State and Local Government program.

Worked for 25 years as a journalist and columnist for The Northwoods Sporting Journal and other publications, and for nearly a year as executive director of the Sportsman's Alliance of Maine; also worked in commercial food service, nonprofit administration, textiles, and farming.
Served in the Maine House of Representatives from 1996 to 2004, representing Old Town (District 121), and chaired the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife.

Elected Maine Secretary of State by the Legislature in 2004 and served 2005-2011; selected again in 2012 and served 2013-2021. Served as president of the National Association of Secretaries of State from 2010 to 2011.
Finished second in the 2012 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, behind Cynthia Dill.
Elected State Auditor by the Legislature in December 2020, served briefly in 2021, and was selected again on November 14, 2022.

Announced a Democratic primary challenge to Rep. Jared Golden in October 2025; Golden announced in November 2025 he would not seek re-election. Dunlap won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary in a ranked-choice runoff.
Founding board member of the Maine Youth Fish and Game Association and a past member of the University of Maine Board of Visitors and the Bangor Symphony Orchestra board; lives in Old Town, Maine.
